purpose: Model how shared meaning forms, scales, fragments, institutionalizes, persists, becomes extractive or high-control, and can be corrected or repaired.
epistemic_boundaries: A cultural category does not prove membership, motive, coordination, criminality or moral quality.
Shared audience or ideology does not establish common command.
Prestige is not truth, reach or moral superiority.
High-control claims require feature-level evidence rather than label-first inference.
Historical labels are dated relationships, not permanent intrinsic properties.

formation_states.definition: People share an event, object, place or recurring interaction.
A small group develops repeated language, norms, jokes, rituals or expectations.
Participation becomes recognizable around venues, creators, practices or media.
A formation develops stronger identity, boundaries, insider knowledge and durable practices.
Participants create alternative channels of discussion, interpretation or legitimacy relative to a wider public.
Culture begins producing durable organizations, campaigns, leadership or coordinated action.
Rules, professions, budgets, organizations and procedures reproduce the formation.
Forms gain wide reach through established distribution and public recognition.
Institutions preserve, teach, award, archive or treat works and practices as exemplary or enduring.
A formation persists across generations and becomes material later cultures inherit, remix, contest or revive.

cultural_dimensions.reach: intimate to mass exposure and participation
cultural_dimensions.participation_depth: exposure, audience, occasional, active, self-identification, formal membership, core production or leadership
cultural_dimensions.boundary_strength: insider vocabulary, initiation, status markers, shibboleths, credentials, rituals and outsider categories
cultural_dimensions.boundary_permeability: capacity to join, leave, disagree or participate partially
cultural_dimensions.institutionalization: reproduction through organizations, rules, funding, professions, education, archives or law
cultural_dimensions.prestige: symbolic status conferred by institutions and gatekeepers
cultural_dimensions.commerciality: dependence on markets, sponsorship, advertising, patronage or platform economies
cultural_dimensions.coercion_exit_cost: social, economic, reputational or practical cost of dissent and departure
cultural_dimensions.archive_persistence: durability, searchability and reproducibility of traces
cultural_dimensions.correctability: capacity to revise false claims, preserve counterevidence, forgive, expire labels and restore reputation
cultural_dimensions.generativity: capacity to produce new works, skills, institutions, relations or capabilities
cultural_dimensions.garden_repair_value: project-normative measure of agency, reciprocity, protection, truth-seeking, meaningful exit and future capacity

popular-culture.definition: Culture with broad audience recognition or participation; popularity describes reach, not inferiority.

mass-culture.definition: Culture produced or distributed through large-scale industrial or platform systems.

high-culture.definition: Culture institutionally treated as prestigious, exemplary or refined; a prestige/canon relation rather than proof of greater human worth.

elite-culture.definition: Practices, tastes or networks concentrated among high-status or high-resource groups; related to but not identical with high culture.

canonical-culture.definition: Works, practices or ideas repeatedly preserved and taught as culturally important.

zeitgeist.definition: A retrospective or analytical description of concerns, styles, technologies, anxieties, hopes, conflicts, symbols and assumptions especially salient in a period; not a mystical causal force.

peak-culture.definition: A formation or moment with unusually high combined cultural generativity and coherence. It is separate from moral quality.

ideal-culture.definition: An explicit normative aspiration describing what a culture says human relations ought to become; compare declared ideals with observable practice.

conflict-culture.definition: A dispute that develops recurring stories, roles, vocabulary, archives, rituals, status systems and institutions that reproduce the conflict.

cultural-repair.definition: Processes that increase correction, accountability, proportion, exit, protection, reciprocity and future capacity.

transformation_models.formation: interaction -> repetition -> shared meaning -> norm -> identity -> memory -> institution -> inheritance or mutation
transformation_models.conflict: incident -> story -> roles -> allies -> vocabulary -> evidence archive -> status system -> recurring rituals -> institution or legal process -> inherited memory
transformation_models.reputation: event or claim -> framing -> repetition -> audience adoption -> archive persistence -> counterclaim -> platform amplification -> professional intervention -> legal or institutional response -> correction, adjudication or unresolved memory
transformation_models.zeitgeist: historical conditions + technologies + institutions + shocks + repeated symbols + public mood + creative response -> recognizable period pattern

project_mapping.sektur: project-defined semi-bounded conflict and attention territory; keep historical Da Sektur distinct from the later Timic generalization
project_mapping.farm: project analytical model of recurring attention cultivation and extraction
project_mapping.swamp: project metaphor for dense, blocked or opaque overlap among incentives, institutions, media, markets and unresolved residue
project_mapping.tree-of-strife: root incentive -> mechanism -> relation -> event -> consequence -> seed of recurrence
project_mapping.garden: project counter-model emphasizing correction, accountability, exit, protection, reciprocity and independent future growth
